title: TCS Subsidiary Plans $7.4 Billion AI Data Center Campus in Hyderabad
excerpt: HyperVault, a TCS unit, has secured 264 acres in Telangana for a 1-gigawatt facility targeting AI companies and hyperscalers.
body:
• TCS subsidiary HyperVault and its partners will invest up to ₹700 billion ($7.41 billion) to build a 1-gigawatt AI data center campus in Hyderabad.
  • The project, spread over 264 acres in Telangana, will be developed in phases and is aimed at AI companies and hyperscalers needing high-density GPU deployments.
  • At full buildout, the campus is expected to rank among India's largest AI infrastructure facilities.
  • The move marks a strategic shift for TCS from its traditional capex-light model, raising questions among analysts about its impact on return ratios.

A subsidiary of Tata Consultancy Services and its partners will invest up to 700 billion rupees ($7.41 billion) to build a 1-gigawatt AI data center campus in Telangana, the company announced on Saturday. The project represents one of India's largest private infrastructure bets on artificial intelligence.

TCS's subsidiary HyperVault has secured 264 acres in Hyderabad for the campus, which will be developed in phases and target AI companies and hyperscalers requiring high-density GPU deployments for AI training and inference workloads, according to Reuters.

Scale and Ambition

At full buildout, HyperVault said the facility is expected to rank among India's largest AI infrastructure projects. The 1-gigawatt capacity target puts it in the same league as major data center campuses being built by global hyperscalers in the United States and Southeast Asia.

"TCS has historically operated on a capex-light, organic growth model that delivered return on equity above 51% and return on invested capital above 80% in FY25."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wBgW4ep2ofY

TCS CEO K Krithivasan said Hyderabad offered the scale, talent, and ecosystem needed to serve global customers. Telangana has emerged as a hub for data center development, with its established IT corridor, reliable power infrastructure, and proximity to a large pool of skilled workers.

The announcement came days after TCS agreed to acquire Porsche AG's automotive and consulting unit MHP, signaling a broader strategy of diversification beyond traditional IT services.

A Strategic Shift — and Its Risks

The data center investment marks a significant departure for India's largest IT services company. TCS has historically operated on a capex-light, organic growth model that delivered return on equity above 51% and return on invested capital above 80% in FY25.

Analysts have raised concerns about the shift. PhillipCapital analyst Karan Uppal warned that the move "effectively moves away from capex-light to capex-intensive business" and could pressure TCS's return ratios. BOBCaps analysts called the plan "negatively surprising," estimating the AI data center business could generate ROE in the teens — far below the company's core business.

TCS shares fell as much as 1.5% following the announcement, reflecting investor caution about capital allocation.

India's Data Center Boom

The investment comes amid an unprecedented data center building boom in India, driven by the surge in AI workloads and the government's push for data localization. Major global players including AWS, Google, and Microsoft have announced or expanded data center operations in India, while domestic players are racing to capture demand.

TCS expects to reach the full 1-gigawatt capacity within five to seven years. The company has not disclosed its financial partners for the project, though the total setup cost was estimated at $6-7 billion.

What to Watch

For TCS shareholders, the key question is whether the AI infrastructure business can generate returns that justify the capital commitment. The company's more proactive M&A stance — including the MHP acquisition — could reduce free cash flow available for shareholder distributions. For India's tech ecosystem, the campus represents a potential anchor for AI development that could attract global AI companies to set up operations in Hyderabad.
